title: Not-for-Profit Financial Statements
description: Understand the statement of financial position, statement of activities, and statement of cash flows.
html:
Core NFP Financial Statements

A not-for-profit organization generally presents financial statements designed to show its financial position, changes in net assets, and cash flows.

  • Statement of Financial Position
  • Statement of Activities
  • Statement of Cash Flows
  • Analysis of expenses by function and nature

Statement of Financial Position

The statement of financial position is similar in purpose to a business entity's balance sheet.

It reports:

ASSETS − LIABILITIES = NET ASSETS

Net assets are presented using the two classifications we already learned.

Net Assets Without Donor Restrictions No Donor-Imposed Restriction
Net Assets With Donor Restrictions Donor-Imposed Restriction

Example — Financial Position

Assume an NFP reports:

Total Assets $900,000
Total Liabilities $260,000
$900,000 − $260,000 = $640,000 TOTAL NET ASSETS

Statement of Activities

The statement of activities reports the organization's revenues, gains, expenses, losses, and other changes in net assets during the reporting period.

BEGINNING NET ASSETS + CHANGE IN NET ASSETS = ENDING NET ASSETS

Changes in Both Net Asset Classes

The statement of activities reports changes separately for:

  • Net assets without donor restrictions
  • Net assets with donor restrictions

Contribution Example

During the year, an NFP receives:

Contribution With No Donor Restriction $80,000
Contribution Restricted for Scholarships $120,000

Both amounts affect the statement of activities, but they affect different net asset classes.

$80,000 → WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS $120,000 → WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Expenses

Expenses are generally reported as decreases in net assets without donor restrictions.

When donor-restricted resources are used for their intended purpose, the related restriction may be released.

EXPENSES → GENERALLY DECREASE NET ASSETS WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Statement of Cash Flows

The statement of cash flows explains changes in cash and cash equivalents during the period.

Cash flows are generally classified among operating, investing, and financing activities.

Operating Day-to-Day Activities
Investing Investments and Long-Lived Assets
Financing Certain Financing Activities

Donor-Restricted Cash Flows

Be careful with contributions containing donor restrictions.

The cash-flow classification depends on the nature and donor stipulations associated with the contribution.

Example

A donor contributes cash specifically restricted for the acquisition of a long-lived asset.

The donor restriction can affect how the cash receipt is classified in the statement of cash flows.

Expenses by Function

Functional classification explains why resources were consumed.

Program Services Mission-Related Activities
Management & General Supporting Activity
Fundraising Supporting Activity

Expenses by Nature

Natural classification explains what type of expense was incurred.

  • Salaries
  • Rent
  • Utilities
  • Supplies
  • Depreciation

Function vs. Nature

FUNCTION = WHY WAS THE MONEY SPENT? NATURE = WHAT TYPE OF COST WAS IT?
Example

A social-service charity pays $70,000 of salaries to employees working directly in its food-assistance program.

Nature Salaries
Function Program Services

Statement Relationships

STATEMENT OF FINANCIAL POSITION → WHERE THE NFP STANDS STATEMENT OF ACTIVITIES → HOW NET ASSETS CHANGED STATEMENT OF CASH FLOWS → WHY CASH CHANGED

CPA Memory Rule

POSITION ASSETS = LIABILITIES + NET ASSETS ACTIVITIES = CHANGE IN NET ASSETS CASH FLOWS = CHANGE IN CASH

Key Takeaways

  • The statement of financial position reports assets, liabilities, and net assets.
  • The statement of activities reports changes in net assets.
  • NFPs distinguish net assets with and without donor restrictions.
  • Expenses generally decrease net assets without donor restrictions.
  • Expense information is analyzed by both function and nature.

quiz.prompt: Which financial statement of a not-for-profit organization primarily reports revenues, expenses, gains, losses, and the resulting changes in net assets during a period?
quiz.explanation: The statement of activities reports revenues, expenses, gains, losses, and other changes that explain the change in the NFP's net assets during the reporting period.

objectives: Explain not-for-profit financial statements and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
Evaluate common errors and their financial-statement effects.
